title: Decoupled metric-producer sidecar for inference latency and KV cache bucketing
creator: Samir Gupta
description: Introduce a lightweight, decoupled 'metric-producer' sidecar process that runs alongside inference workers to standardize emission of Prometheus-friendly metrics and OTLP spans for custom inference KPIs (per-request token counts, KV cache hit buckets, model-variant routing counts, latency percentiles with exemplar IDs). The sidecar centralizes aggregation windows (per-request vs per-minute), enforces label cardinality rules, and applies tenant-aware rate limiting so downstream ingestion (OTel collector / Prometheus pushgateway) remains stable under bursty traffic. This reduces request-side overhead, avoids per-request blocking I/O, and provides a single exchange point for schema transformation and tenant tagging.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Sidecar binary built and deployable via existing pod template; 2) Emits the following metrics in Prometheus format: redwood_inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket (with stable labels), redwood_kv_cache_hit_ratio_bucketed, redwood_model_routing_total; 3) Exposes OTLP exporter configuration with TLS and tenant header pass-through; 4) Demonstrated end-to-end flow: inference request -> sidecar aggregation -> otel-collector -> prometheus remote write with no P99 latency regression (>5%); 5) Integration test that simulates 10k rps burst and verifies no high-cardinality labels created and backpressure applied to exporter.
implementation_notes: Architecture: sidecar collects structured per-request metric events over a local unix socket/HTTP endpoint from the main worker (non-blocking). It buffers and aggregates using fixed windows, applies cardinality policy (label whitelist + hash-bucketing for user_id), and emits both OTLP (for long-term storage) and Prometheus exposition for local scraping. Key opts: adjustable aggregation window, max label cardinality per-metric, adaptive emission on exporter error (exponential backoff) and a local ring buffer for critical events. Use existing otel-go SDK for exporter plumbing and reuse the runtime's tenant header propagation. We will implement a small shim in the worker to send minimal envelope: {metric_name, value, labels, exemplar_id}.
notes: Avoid introducing high-cardinality labels like full prompt hashes. For tenant-specific metrics, prefer aggregate tenant_id buckets. Measure cost of exemplar retention separately. Consider later adding a light-weight sampling policy driven by tracing hints (error-only exemplars).
comments: 2026-01-30 - Samir Gupta: Spike completed. Sidecar prototype collects events over unix domain socket and aggregates into 500ms windows. Memory overhead under 50MB for typical worker process.
2026-02-05 - Ava Martinez: Reviewed prototype. Requested changes: add configuration for label whitelist per-deployment and document behavior when exporter returns 429/5xx.
2026-02-12 - Samir Gupta: Implemented adaptive backoff + ring buffer for 10k events. Added unit tests for bucketing user_id to stable 64 buckets to control cardinality.

2026-02-20 - Leah O'Connor (PM): Confirmed SLO for ingestion: end-to-end P99 latency must not increase by more than 5% after sidecar rollout. Also requested a visible switch in Console to disable sidecar metrics per-customer.

2026-02-28 - Ops: During small internal load test we saw a spike in OTLP exporter errors when remote write throttled; sidecar successfully backed off and buffered. Need to add alerting when buffer exceeds 80% capacity.

2026-03-04 - Ava Martinez: Integration test harness updated to simulate high-cardinality attacker pattern. Sidecar bucketing reduced label cardinality to expected bounds. Ready for staging deployment.
2026-03-05 - Samir Gupta: Merged initial PRs to feature branch. Next: run canary on dedicated infra and validate console dashboards (latency/error) for baselining.
testing_plan: 1) Unit tests for aggregation windows and bucketing logic; 2) Integration test with otel-collector and Prometheus remote write using our staging stack; 3) Load test: 10k rps with synthetic tenant distribution, verify memory/CPU and exporter backpressure; 4) Canary rollout on 2 clusters for 24h with telemetry SLI comparison to baseline.
rollout_steps: 1) Deploy sidecar as opt-in in staging; 2) Canary on dedicated runtime pool (5% traffic); 3) Monitor SLO/ingestion errors for 72h; 4) Gradual ramp to 100% on non-sensitive tenants; 5) Enable per-tenant toggle in Console and plan enterprise communication.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: accidental high-cardinality labels leading to ingestion blowup. Mitigation: enforced whitelist and deterministic bucketing, default deny for unknown labels. Risk: increased CPU on workers due to IPC overhead. Mitigation: non-blocking socket + batching and ability to disable sidecar emission at runtime.
audit_trail: Created by Samir Gupta 2026-01-28. Prototype spikes, reviews, and PRs documented in comments. Security signoff not required for MVP; will loop in security for enterprise rollout.
